- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, indicating an overshoot after spikes followed by premature mean reversion.
- Model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–10 days) in most cases, suggesting a lag in capturing sustained upward momentum or policy-driven price increases.
- Forecasts show a tendency to smooth out volatility, underreacting to sharp price spikes in the history, leading to underestimation of true price movements.
- Model exhibits a strong bias toward higher values in the middle of the forecast horizon (days 15–25), possibly due to overconfidence in recent trends or failure to account for seasonal or regulatory adjustments.
- When true prices rise sharply (e.g., >10% from prior day), model forecasts often fail to catch the momentum, leading to underestimation.
- Model tends to underestimate prices during periods of high regulatory or policy uncertainty, suggesting it underweights external shocks.
- Forecasts often fail to account for the lag between policy announcements and market reaction, leading to delayed price adjustments in the model.
